nodes.label: Basic circle terms and radii
nodes.description: Identify and use the basic terms of the circle (centre, radius, chord, diameter, surface of the circle, points inside, on and outside) and use radii and diameters to compare lengths and solve problems.

nodes.label: Axes of symmetry in circle
nodes.description: Describe the axes of symmetry of a circle and state that any straight line through the centre is an axis of symmetry.

nodes.label: Chord–centre perpendicular corollaries
nodes.description: Apply the corollaries relating the centre, a chord and its midpoint or perpendicular to calculate lengths, angles and areas and to prove statements about chords.

nodes.label: Position of a point relative to a circle
nodes.description: Determine the position of a point with respect to a circle by comparing MA with the radius r, and find unknown values (x) from such conditions.

nodes.label: Line and circle; tangents
nodes.description: Determine whether a straight line is outside, a secant or a tangent to a circle by comparing the distance MA with the radius r, and use the perpendicularity of a tangent to the radius at the point of tangency to calculate lengths and angles and to justify that a line is a tangent.

nodes.label: Position of two circles
nodes.description: Determine the position of two circles (distant, touching externally or internally, intersecting, concentric) by comparing MN with r_1 + r_2 and r_1 - r_2.

nodes.label: Line of centers applications
nodes.description: Use the line of centers of touching or intersecting circles, with the common tangent and the common chord, to calculate lengths and angles and to prove relations.

nodes.label: Circle through one point
nodes.description: Draw circles passing through a given point, choosing centers and using the compass, and state that infinitely many such circles exist (equal radii give centers on a congruent circle centered at A).

nodes.label: Circle through two points
nodes.description: Draw circles passing through two given points using the axis of the chord AB for the center, and determine the possible circles for a given radius or diameter, including the smallest radius.

nodes.label: Circle through three points
nodes.description: Draw the circumcircle through three noncollinear points as the intersection of the axes of two sides, identify its center in the triangle, and explain why collinear points give no circle.

nodes.label: Chord length versus distance
nodes.description: Compare the lengths of chords of a circle with their distances from the center, using >, < and =, and find the range of a value from such a comparison.

nodes.label: Equal chords are equidistant
nodes.description: Use the theorem that equal chords are equidistant from the center (also in congruent circles) to find lengths and angles and to prove equalities.

nodes.label: Converse: equidistant chords are equal
nodes.description: Use the converse of the theorem, that chords equidistant from the center(s) are equal in length, to calculate chord lengths and prove chords equal, including in concentric and intersecting circles.
